solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A blighter splitting note in amusement centre

indicators.note: a piece that splits another goes into the middle of it, so the blighter sits within the note

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a cad is a rotter or blighter

explanation.surface: Some unpleasant fellow is muscling in somewhere among the slot machines at the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blighter' is old British slang for a contemptible man, which is also what a cad is.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an amusement arcade is a hall full of games and slot machines.

clue.text: Trickery in case of diamonds found under craft

indicators.note: in a down clue the later pieces sit beneath the craft

parts.note: art is skill or craft
if means in the event of
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: Deception in a jewel case reveals stones hidden beneath a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' and 'craft' suggest a box and a vessel, but 'in case of' is IF and 'craft' is ART. ICE is slang for diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: Artifice means clever deception or cunning tricks.

clue.text: Interest created by leader of crusade performing church service

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: on means performing, as an actor on stage
CE is the Church of England
RN, the Royal Navy, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A crusader's chief draws attention by conducting a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' here is a branch of the armed forces, not worship: RN is the Royal Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a matter of interest to someone is a concern of theirs.

clue.text: Head of department to study fear

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university

explanation.surface: A department boss sits down to examine what frightens people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of department' sounds like a person but just gives D.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: dread is great fear or apprehension.

clue.text: Eastern hamper curiously containing English objects of no lasting value

parts.note: E is the standard abbreviation for east or eastern

indicators.note: the rearranged hamper holds the next piece inside itself
done curiously, the letters of the word hamper are set out in an odd new order

explanation.surface: An oriental picnic basket, oddly, is packed with English trinkets that won't last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curiously' turns HAMPER into PHMERA, and 'containing' puts E inside it to give PHEMERA, after the first E.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemera are things, often printed matter, meant to be used briefly and then thrown away.

clue.text: Foreboding — tense soldiers consumed by it

parts.note: the present is a grammatical tense

indicators.note: something consumed by another is swallowed inside it

parts.note: men are soldiers, the other ranks

explanation.surface: Nervous troops are overcome by a sense of something bad coming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' looks like an adjective describing soldiers but is the grammatical present tense.
explanation.definitionFit: A presentiment is an intuitive feeling that something, usually unpleasant, will happen.

clue.text: Denied row involved quilt

indicators.note: involved means intricate or tangled, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone refused to be dragged into an argument over the bedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges DENIED ROW.
explanation.definitionFit: An eiderdown is a thick bed cover filled with down feathers.

clue.text: Weird tales about the Spanish girl in Great Expectations

indicators.note: about means around, so the scrambled tales goes round the next piece
weird means strange, so the letters of tales take an odd new order

parts.note: el is the Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Strange stories surround a Spanish girl from a Dickens novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weird' marks the anagram and 'about' wraps it round the Spanish word for 'the'; the girl is Pip's love in the Dickens novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Estella is the cold, beautiful ward of Miss Havisham whom Pip loves in Dickens's novel.

clue.text: Indifference, in a way, over play's ending

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece over another is placed above it

parts.note: a path is a way

indicators.note: the ending of the word play means its final letter is taken

explanation.surface: A spectator shrugs off how the play turned out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' places A PATH above Y in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Apathy is a lack of interest, enthusiasm or concern.

clue.text: Listen out for something associated with Christmas?

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of listen are put out of order

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep your ears open for something festive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the letters of LISTEN. The question mark marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Glittery decorative strips are hung on trees during the festive season, so they are a seasonal example.

clue.text: Feud heralds demise for all in Meditteranean capital

indicators.note: one word standing in for another signals a swap of letters inside the capital

parts.note: Valletta is the capital of Malta, in the Mediterranean (the clue misspells the sea)
taken as written
demise means death, an end

explanation.surface: A quarrel brings about everyone's downfall in some southern European city.
explanation.walkthrough: In VALLETTA the letters ALL are replaced by END. 'Meditteranean' is a misspelling in the printed clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendetta is a long, bitter quarrel, often a blood feud between families.

clue.text: Tablet sadly crushed in field

indicators.note: sadly suggests things gone awry, so the letters of tablet are jumbled

parts.note: ground means crushed, as with coffee beans

explanation.surface: A pill is unhappily pulverised out in a meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges TABLET to BATTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A field of battle is a battleground, and figuratively any area of conflict.

clue.text: Put out food for a type of thrush

parts.note: to field in cricket is to put out a team to catch and stop the ball
fare is food served

explanation.surface: Someone leaves scraps on the bird table for a passing thrush.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'field' a side in cricket or football is to put them out on the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: The fieldfare is a large grey-headed thrush that winters in Britain.

clue.text: Boy in river, sacred one

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river
Alph is the sacred river in Coleridge's poem Kubla Khan

explanation.surface: A lad is taking a dip in a holy river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Where Alph, the sacred river, ran' is a line from Coleridge's Kubla Khan, so 'sacred one' (river) gives ALPH.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph is a male first name, so it can stand for a boy.

clue.text: Make-up a student put on for a walk

parts.note: one's constitution is one's make-up or physical nature
L, for learner, stands for a student, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A student puts on cosmetics before going out for a stroll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make-up' looks cosmetic but means physical nature.
explanation.definitionFit: A constitutional is a brisk walk taken for the sake of one's health.

clue.text: He's enthralled by sign in reference book

indicators.note: held captive by, so the first words go inside the sign

parts.note: Taurus, the bull, is a sign of the zodiac
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A man is captivated by an omen he finds in a dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sign' is a zodiac sign, not an omen; the apostrophe in He's is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesaurus is a book listing words grouped by similar meaning, consulted for reference.

clue.text: Member of police force getting info on lady touring centre of Paris

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the lady surrounds the next letter

parts.note: a dame is a titled lady

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter

explanation.surface: A French officer is briefed on a woman visiting the heart of Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' puts R, the middle letter of Paris, inside DAME.
explanation.definitionFit: A gendarme is a French policeman, a member of the national police force.

clue.text: Indefinite number inhabiting Aberdeen — limit unfortunately cannot be ascertained

indicators.note: living inside, so the number goes within the jumbled city and limit
unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: n is the mathematician's symbol for an unspecified number

explanation.surface: An unspecified number of people live in Aberdeen, and sadly its boundary can't be fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' marks the anagram of the city plus the boundary word, and 'inhabiting' sets the indefinite number inside it; the dash hides that the definition is the last three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Something indeterminable is impossible to settle or establish exactly.

clue.text: Carved toggle teens twirled across UK

indicators.note: the jumbled letters stretch across the next piece, holding it within
twirled means spun round, so the letters of teens are set out afresh

explanation.surface: Teenagers spin a decorative fastener round the country.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled letters of the teens split around the country's abbreviation, NETS before it and E after.
explanation.definitionFit: A netsuke is a carved Japanese ornament used as a toggle to hang items from a kimono sash.

clue.text: Personal attendant pressing whites, finally, for Bradman, say

indicators.note: pressing means squeezing, so the attendant clasps the following letter

parts.note: a batman is an officer's personal servant in the British army

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A valet ironing cricket whites, at last, for the great Australian player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pressing' puts S, the last letter of whites, inside BATMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Don Bradman, the great Australian cricketer, is an example of a batter.

clue.text: Set off in race holding record

indicators.note: the race holds the record, which goes inside it

parts.note: to dart is to race or dash
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: An athlete in a race begins while still clutching a vinyl disc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race' is a verb here, to dash, not a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to set off on a journey is to leave or go away.

clue.text: No ball, perhaps, in over

definitions.meaning: in cricket a no-ball is one of the runs credited to the batting side without being scored off the bat, like a wide or bye
over in the sense of additional, more than needed

explanation.surface: A cricket umpire calls an illegal delivery during an over.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is a set of six balls in cricket; here it means surplus.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket's runs not scored off the bat carry this name, and the word also means surplus or additional.

clue.text: Gave a facelift to a Denver resort

indicators.note: to re-sort is to sort again, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone smartened up a holiday resort in Colorado.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday spot but is read as re-sort, rearranging TO A DENVER.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a building a facelift is to restore and refurbish it.

clue.text: Clear crypt

definitions.meaning: to clear a fence or bar is to leap over it

explanation.surface: Tidy up a burial chamber beneath a church.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to leap over an obstacle and an arched underground chamber for burial.

clue.text: Song from Hair stars

definitions.meaning: the opening number of the rock musical Hair, 'Age of' the water carrier
the constellation of the water carrier, a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A number from a musical, performed by its leading actors.
explanation.walkthrough: Hair is a 1960s rock musical whose opening song is this title.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a famous song from the musical and a zodiac constellation of stars.

clue.text: Oceanic bird saved by resourceful marine

indicators.note: the bird is kept safe inside the words resourceful marine

explanation.surface: A seabird in trouble is rescued by a quick-thinking marine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saved by' signals letters held within resourceFUL MARine.
explanation.definitionFit: The fulmar is a grey and white seabird of the petrel family.

clue.text: Industrial region, seediest, for redevelopment

indicators.note: redevelopment rebuilds, so the letters of seediest are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: The shabbiest manufacturing district is earmarked for regeneration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for redevelopment' rearranges SEEDIEST. Teesside is an industrial area of north-east England around Middlesbrough.
explanation.definitionFit: Teesside, round the lower River Tees, was a centre of steel and chemical industry.

clue.text: Example that's missing in policy

indicators.note: the example lacks the short word that follows, so it is removed

parts.note: an instance is an example
taken as written

explanation.surface: An illustration that has fallen out of a political programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's missing' takes IN from INSTANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: One's stance on an issue is one's position or policy on it.
